text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli police, settlers clash in Hebron.
- Multi-sector strike organised by Histadrut labour union federation to hit flights, Bezeq phone company, railways.
- Hizbollah guerrilla footage shows bomb attack.
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: Opposition couldn't run a grocery store.
- Jordan spins web of spies on the Internet.
- Government and British firm Cable & Wireless mull joint control of Israel's Bezeq Communications.
- Israel's Bank Leumi in talks on sale of Ihud Insurance.
GLOBES
- Sharp drop in economic activity in Israel in November after two months of improvement. Commentary: It's a drop following an artificial rise.
- Bezeq phone call rates expected to rise next week by 3.23 percent.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu asks to accelerate negotiations on the "final status" with Palestinians, so as not to hand over wide stretches of territory.
- Islamic Trust, the Waqf, begins construction without permit on Temple Mount; challenge to be presented today to High Court of Justice.
- New compensation from Germany for Holocaust survivors compensated once at the start of the 1950s.
- Environment Ministry demands closing the centre of Tel Aviv to cars so that air pollution can pass standards.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu in steamroller press to halt opposition to agreement. Still a majority in the government but criticism of decision-making process on the rise.
- Thefts in Israel's Knesset: VCRs and televisions disappear from offices of parliament members.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Syria feared a blow in the Golan and Israel says in calming message: "We'll not attack."
- Should the prime minister have made public his commitments to Habad?
- Israel's Egged Bus Co to halt 15-year-old line 100 to Cairo because of losses.
